caption:
In 2020 we did what a lot of people did. We bought a new house in the middle of the pandemic…you know, the one where homes were selling for numbers that felt unbelievable at the time?

Low interest rates, remote work, and a wave of buyers hit the market all at once.

We bought, renovated, settled in and we love our house.  But like a lot of homeowners, I think we all quietly started believing those prices were the new baseline.

The market has shifted since then and right now one of the biggest conversations in real estate is the gap between what homeowners think their home is worth and what buyers will actually pay.

I became a realtor this year, so I decided to stop wondering and run a CMA on our own house. A Comparative Market Analysis is basically what realtors use to estimate a home’s value based on recent sales. 🤓👌

Follow along on @yowcitysold because I’m sharing that number and what I think every Ottawa pandemic buyer should understand about today’s market.

Were you a pandemic purchaser too? How has the ride been since? 👇

📸 @kamaramorozukphoto

RECIPE

• 1 chunk of ginger
• 3 pitted dates
• Sprinkle of cinnamon
• Splash of vanilla
• 1 tbsp high-quality olive oil 
• 1 tbsp honey or maple syrup
• 4–5 ice cubes
• 1 cup water

caption:
A few tips if you’re heading to see Coldplay at the Rogers Stadium in Toronto:⁣
⁣
✨ Wear comfy shoes - the walk in to the venue feels like a pre-concert pilgrimage and there is lots of grass and gravel to cross once there. ⁣
✨Small purses and fanny packs are allowed. ⁣
✨ There is no roof so be prepared for the weather. I was happy to have an extra layer once the sun went down. ⁣
✨ Bring a refillable water bottle (1L or smaller) for the water stations.⁣
✨Lines for merch were long but food and drink was pretty speedy. Drinks are pricey (approx $20 with tax and tip each).⁣
✨Entering and leaving wasn’t as terrible as expected. Crowd control was well done on night 2.⁣
✨ Coldplay is scheduled to start at 8:45pm. ⁣
✨ Research the set list to time your washroom/drink refill breaks. ⁣
✨ The tour aims to be as sustainable as possible so don’t forget to recycle your bracelet in the bins when leaving. ⁣
✨ There are no hotels nearby. We stayed at a Marriot in Vaughan.⁣
✨ Be prepared to feel feelings…seriously, they know how to hit you right in the soul. Bring tissues! ⁣
⁣
Thank you, Coldplay, for reminding us what it feels like to be fully present, fully human, and fully lit up - inside and out. 🫶✨

caption:
How amazing would it be to win a trip to Hawaii?!!!🧳✈️ ⁣
⁣
The @FriendlyFutureFoundation Sweepstakes closes November 30th, with 100% of the proceeds going to the @TELUS Student Bursary program, which supports over 500 students each year, who are facing financial barriers and making a difference in their community! ⁣
⁣
Don’t miss out and head to the link in my bio to enter. In the meantime, here’s how you can make your own tunapoke bowls at home to get your aloha vibes flowing!#telus_partner⁣
⁣
𝗧𝘂𝗻𝗮 𝗣𝗼𝗸𝗲 𝗕𝗼𝘄𝗹 𝗥𝗲𝗰𝗶𝗽𝗲 🍣🌿 (makes 2)⁣
⁣
𝗜𝗻𝗴𝗿𝗲𝗱𝗶𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀:⁣
1 lb sushi-grade tuna, cubed⁣
2 cups cooked rice⁣
1/4 cup soy sauce⁣
1 tbsp sesame oil⁣
1 tbsp rice vinegar⁣
1 tsp of chili flakes (optional)⁣
2 tsp sesame seeds⁣
Green onions, thinly sliced⁣
Sriracha or spicy mayo for a kick! 🔥⁣
your choice of fresh toppings: sliced cucumbers, shredded red cabbage, edamame, matchstick carrots, sliced avocado, pickled ginger, seaweed salad...get creative!⁣
⁣
𝗜𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀:⁣
1. Mix soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and chili flakes in a bowl.⁣
2. Toss tuna cubes in the mixture and let marinate for 10-15 minutes.⁣
3. Assemble your bowl: rice on the bottom, then top with tuna and your fave toppings.⁣
4. Drizzle some spicy mayo and sprinkle with sesame seeds.⁣
5. Enter the TELUS Friendly Future Sweepstakes and enjoy ;)⁣

#𝘈𝘭𝘤𝘰𝘯_𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘵𝘯𝘦𝘳 It’s a rite of passage realizing that the ones who took care of us eventually need us to take care of them, and this is something I’m starting to experience as my parents approach their 80s. I stay on top of my own eye health with regular optometrist exams and I’m glad I recently encouraged my dad to do the same because we learned that not only did he need glasses but we also discovered the early signs of cataracts. Cataracts are a very common and natural part of aging, and there are choices when it comes to your vision to help make sure we continue to live our best lives. My dad and I now have a standing annual date to go to the optometrist together and have learned more about cataracts to explore his options for down the road at seethefullpicture.myalcon.com ⁣
 (𝘭𝘪𝘯𝘬 𝘪𝘯 𝘣𝘪𝘰). My two big takeaways: Information is power when it comes to our health and be sure to take care of the ones who took care of you.

Looking back to learn, moving forward to evolve. Wishing you all a year full of wins you’re working towards. Giddy up, 2025! 🙌
